hotContext.criticalNews: Texas registration pipeline jumped ~50% in one day to 175 Model Y robotaxis, but commercial service remains Model Y–based, Cybercab is still not in paid unsupervised fleets, Miami ops show tiny geofence and reliability quirks, and accessibility is a lobbying claim without a product date.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla registers 58 more Model Y robotaxis in Texas — fleet to 175 in one day
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 15, 2026, Tesla Robotaxi LLC added 58 Model Y vehicles to Texas's automated-vehicle registry in a single day, lifting the company's Texas-registered robotaxi pool from 117 to 175 (~50% overnight). Texas Autonomous Vehicle Tracker, TeslaNorth, Basenor, and EVXL all corroborate the DMV-based jump — the largest one-day registration step visible on the public tracker. Dallas Tesla Club cross-checked VINs against the state registry. Competitive context: Waymo still leads Texas registrations at 642, Avride at 317, Tesla at 175, Zoox at 44. Critical caveat: registration is inventory/authorization pipeline, not proven rider-serving capacity. Service still runs on Model Y, not production Cybercab; software/safety constraints — not car availability — remain the binding limit. Hot-context active commercial fleet was ~20 vehicles across cities; a registration surge does not by itself reverse year-long scaling failure if unsupervised utilization stays thin.

positive_signals: Largest single-day Texas robotaxi registration increase on public tracker (+58 Model Y)
Texas registered pool now 175 vehicles (up from 117 on July 14)
Multi-source corroboration: Texas AV Tracker, TeslaNorth, Basenor, EVXL; Dallas Tesla Club VIN check
Shows Tesla still batching fleet intake rather than freezing expansion
negative_signals: Registration ≠ active rider-serving fleet; prior active commercial fleet still ~20 vehicles after ~1 year
All 58 additions are Model Y — purpose-built Cybercab still not in commercial robotaxi service
Tesla remains 3rd in Texas AV registrations: Waymo 642, Avride 317, Tesla 175, Zoox 44
Software/safety constraint on unsupervised FSD still the bottleneck, not vehicle count
No disclosure of which cities get the new units or when they enter paid unsupervised service

key_metrics.actual: 175 Texas-registered Tesla robotaxi vehicles (+58 on July 15; prior day 117)
key_metrics.target: Mass-market unsupervised robotaxi scale; 1M robotaxi compensation milestone
key_metrics.trajectory: Registration pipeline accelerating in batches; commercial utilization and Cybercab deployment still lag

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla claims wheelchair-accessible robotaxi 'active product' in Texas — no timeline
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 13, 2026, Tesla Senior Policy Advisor India Herdman told the Washington D.C. City Council that Tesla is 'in development for a purpose-built, wheelchair-accessible autonomous vehicle' being built in Texas, citing paratransit difficulty and permanent wheelchair users' need for free movement. Covered by Wired, Teslarati, and Electrek. No model name, specs, or launch date given. Current commercial robotaxi fleet is Model Y (not wheelchair-accessible); production Cybercab is also not wheelchair-accessible (only braille controls and transfer-height seating). Herdman did not say whether this is the long-stalled Robovan or a new body style. Claim was made while lobbying on a DC bill that could allow robotaxi operations — not as an engineering milestone. Waymo also admitted at the same hearing it has no fully wheelchair-accessible driverless platform. ADA/DOJ pressure on ride-hail accessibility is rising (DOJ sued Uber in Sept 2025).

positive_signals: First on-record confirmation from Tesla policy staff that a wheelchair-accessible AV is an 'active product' in Texas
Acknowledges paratransit gap and permanent wheelchair users as a product requirement
Consistent with Musk 'Absolutely' reply (Sept 2025) and Robotaxi app accessibility tab
negative_signals: Zero timeline, specs, chassis identity, or regulatory path disclosed
Made in a DC City Council hearing on robotaxi legislation — policy theater risk, not product launch
Current Model Y robotaxi and Cybercab are not wheelchair-accessible; app still redirects to third-party WAV providers
Robovan has had no public timeline since We, Robot (Oct 2024); claim may just re-label that vaporware
No US robotaxi operator offers fleetwide driverless WAV service — including market leader Waymo
ADA exposure grows as unsupervised service expands without accessible vehicles

key_metrics.actual: Policy statement only; 0 wheelchair-accessible vehicles in Tesla robotaxi fleet
key_metrics.trajectory: Claim without schedule; accessibility remains an unsolved product and regulatory gap

recentKeyChanges.title: Miami robotaxi first rides expose tiny geofence, cancellations, and support interventions
recentKeyChanges.description: More than a week after the July 3 Miami unsupervised launch (already covered in hot context), TeslaOracle published first-impression reporting on July 14 detailing operational friction. Geofence is only ~10–20 square miles (West Miami, parts of Doral/Sweetwater/Coral Gables). YouTubers from The Road to Autonomy and David Moss had rides cancelled twice (lightning + unknown), struggled to get a car due to small fleet vs demand, watched a Model Y arrive then leave without pickup, then sat in a vehicle that would not move until they called Tesla Support via the rear screen. A piece of tree bark on the road froze the car for 4 minutes 45 seconds with no rider disengage option. Positive notes: unsupervised operation with no safety rider, handled flooded streets/puddles, and some local users (e.g. Justin Berman) called the experience better than traditional ride-hail. Reality: geographic expansion without fleet depth produces poor availability and brittle edge-case handling — classic failed-scale pattern.

positive_signals: Unsupervised Model Y robotaxis operating in Miami without onboard safety personnel
Some riders report better experience than traditional ride-share
Handled mildly flooded Miami streets without apparent confusion
negative_signals: Geofence only ~10–20 sq mi — deliberately tiny pilot footprint
Multiple cancellations and failed pickups on early tester rides
Vehicle would not depart until Tesla Support was called — not a hands-off product yet
Bark on road froze robotaxi ~4:45 with no rider override path
Hard to get a car: small fleet vs demand — availability failure, not just software demo
Still Model Y Juniper fleet; Cybercab not in Miami commercial service

key_metrics.actual: Miami unsupervised geofence ~10–20 sq mi; fleet size undisclosed; multi-cancellation tester experience
key_metrics.target: City-scale unsupervised robotaxi with reliable ETAs
key_metrics.trajectory: Geographic logo on the map without density or reliability of a real network
